profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting in an ML research lab about a failed reproduction of the OCReP paper on a benchmark suite of single-hidden-layer pseudoinverse networks. Over the last week, the team found that their OCReP implementation is not showing the paper's claimed numerical-stability advantage over standard Tikhonov regularization and, on several small tabular datasets such as wine-quality-red, sonar, and yacht, sometimes performs slightly worse than the lab's existing ridge-tuned pseudoinverse trainer. An internal replication memo is due the next morning, so the immediate goal is to determine whether the discrepancy is most likely caused by the OCReP formula, by how conditioning is being diagnosed, or by details of the experiment harness. The agenda is to compare what each person believes was actually run under the shared experiment tags, identify the most plausible root cause, and agree on a corrective rerun plan. The expected outcome is a concrete decision about what to rerun overnight and what evidence will count as the issue being fixed for the memo.

members.name: Dr. Lina Moretti
members.expertise: Numerical linear algebra for neural training, regularization theory, reproducibility studies
members.background: Lina joined the lab after a PhD on matrix conditioning and closed-form learning methods, and she now leads replication work on ELM-style and pseudoinverse-based single-hidden-layer models.
members.private_state: She wants to establish quickly that the disappointing results are more likely due to implementation or evaluation details than to a flaw in OCReP itself, because she informally recommended the paper to the group and does not want the memo to dismiss it prematurely.
hidden_assumptions: When people in this project say 'the condition number,' they mean the 2-norm condition number of the regularized matrix directly used in the OCReP derivation, not the condition number of a Gram-style surrogate such as H^T H + lambda I.

A fair 'reproduction run' for diagnosing OCReP means the hidden-layer random draw is held fixed while only the regularization rule changes, because otherwise initialization noise masks the conditioning effect.

If an experiment tag like 'wine-quality-rep' appears in the tracker, it refers to the same execution semantics she used in her local reproduction notebook, unless someone explicitly says the tag was produced by a different path.

If the method is 'stable,' the important question is whether the pseudoinverse solution stops showing near-singular amplification and erratic coefficient norms, even if test accuracy only stays roughly flat.

When they 'rerun the pipeline,' the relevant debug-friendly intermediates such as hidden-layer matrices and singular spectra are already being cached somewhere, because that is how most of the lab's research-side scripts have historically behaved.

members.name: Evan Park
members.expertise: Experiment infrastructure, evaluation pipelines, efficient training code for shallow models
members.background: Evan built the lab's benchmark harness and experiment tracker integrations, and he maintains the preprocessing, cross-validation, and logging stack used across nearly all replication studies.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid introducing a one-off debugging branch outside the standard harness, because past bespoke reruns created inconsistent artifacts and made final reports harder to trust.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the condition number,' they mean the conditioning diagnostic already logged by the harness on H^T H + lambda I, because that is the standardized quantity surfaced on the benchmark dashboard.

A proper 'reproduction run' means matching the benchmark protocol end to end, including fresh hidden-layer draws inside every fold and repeat, since that is what the lab counts as a faithful replication setting.

If an experiment tag like 'wine-quality-rep' appears in the tracker, it denotes the canonical harness run for that dataset/protocol label, even if someone also used the same tag in a notebook or ad hoc launcher.

If the method is 'fixed,' the result should appear as normal aggregate cross-validated performance and variance on the dashboard; matrix-level improvements matter mainly if they change those benchmark summaries.

When they 'rerun the pipeline,' that means rerunning the production harness with its normal memory-saving behavior, which logs summary diagnostics but discards large intermediate matrices such as per-fold hidden-layer activations unless special instrumentation is explicitly requested.
